ov: A small, long-bodied hunter of Eurasia and the northern parts of North America. Its pure white winter coat is called ermine, a fur worn by monarchs and long used on the ceremonial robes of the UK House of Lords.
wt: Males about 258 g, females under 180 g
rg: Eurasia and northern North America; introduced to New Zealand.
df: Mainly mouse-like rodents, plus larger rodents, rabbits, birds, lizards and insects.
fx: Stoats were brought to New Zealand from Britain in the 1880s to control rabbits, and now threaten its native birds.
Males are roughly 25% larger than females.
